title: A resolved QC decision must leave the active queue immediately, via read-side filtering
requirement: Once a QC decision is recorded for an item, that item MUST NOT appear in the default/active queue view on the very next render, for any operator. This MUST be achieved by excluding already-decided ids at read time (e.g. an outer join / anti-join against the decision record, or a filtered id set), not by deleting or mutating the item's live row.
rationale: Uniform across every surveyed Clank with a QC queue: watch-clank's active query outer-joins EventReview and filters where the review id is null; chinese-tech-wire maps every decision to a status outside its active-queue status set; korean-tech-wire and oem-radar and smartwatch-clank and feature-phone-clank and tablet-clank all filter out decided ids read-side; semiconductor-intelligence's query explicitly documents the same anti-join pattern. This also serves STD-UI-COM-002: because the live row is never mutated for QC purposes, the decision record stays the sole source of truth and re-running collection cannot silently un-QC an item.
forbidden: Deleting the live row to remove it from the queue
Flipping a status flag on the live row as the only mechanism removing it from the queue (this conflates operational state with QC state and was explicitly avoided by every surveyed Clank)
A queue view that requires a manual refresh/second click to reflect a just-made decision
acceptance: The active-queue query excludes any item with an existing decision record, computed at read time
No code path deletes or QC-flags the live row as part of submitting a decision

A decision submitted in one request is logically absent from the very next queue query/render — this is a query-time guarantee, not a mandate on any particular frontend rendering technology, transition, or removal-animation timing

evidence.summary: QC_DECISION_TO_LEAD_STATUS maps every decision outside the active-queue status set the default query filters on.
Same read-side anti-join/filter pattern independently present in every other surveyed Clank with a QC queue.

notes: RATIFIED 2026-08-30 by Operator Ratification Decision 001 (decisions/0003-operator-ratification-decision-001.md). Acceptance criterion reworded (editorial, meaning unchanged, no version bump) to make explicit this is a logical/query-level removal guarantee, not a claim about DOM timing or a particular frontend technology. N/A for smartphone-clank (no queue view exists there at all) — not counted as counter-evidence, see docs/gui-ratification-pass-1.md.
